title: UMDP standard constraint set
description: Meta-schema for the machine-readable standard definitions in schema/standards/*.json. A constraint set says, per UMDP field, what the named standard actually DEFINES: a constant it is not the standard without (locked), a bound a spec may make stricter but never looser (bounded), a field the standard leaves to the spec (optional), or one it says must not be stated at all (not_applicable). Every entry carries the clause it comes from and a verbatim quote, so a consumer can check the constraint against the document rather than trusting this file.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier; must equal the filename stem.

name.description: Canonical display name, written into assets.audio.loudness.standards[].name when a profile adopts this standard.

aliases.description: Other spellings that resolve to this standard when matching an existing profile's free-text name (e.g. 'EBU R128' for 'EBU R 128'). Matching is case-insensitive and ignores whitespace; aliases exist so an already-published profile can be recognised, not so new ones can be authored loosely.

edition.description: The exact edition these constraints were read from, e.g. 'R 128-2023 (v5, November 2023)'. A later edition may change a locked constant; the edition is part of the claim.

role.description: 'delivery' — the standard sets values a deliverable must meet. 'measurement' — the standard specifies how to measure and sets no delivery values at all (ITU-R BS.1770). A measurement standard constrains nothing, and naming one does not license a spec to claim its numbers are the standard's.

measured_with.description: Standards this one requires the measurement to be made with.

applies_to.description: Content classes this constraint set governs. Omitted means it governs any content type. R 128 programme and R 128 s1 short-form are different envelopes over the same field set; conflating them is how a commercials tolerance leaks into a programme spec.

supplements.description: id of the standard this one refines for a narrower content class.

fields.description: UMDP field path -> constraint. Path grammar: dot-separated keys from the profile root, with '[]' marking an array whose every element is governed (e.g. assets.audio.loudness.standards[].target).

not_yet_modelled.description: Parameters the standard defines that UMDP has no field for. Recorded so the omission is visible and traceable rather than silently lost; each entry should name the ticket that would add the field.

rule.description: 'locked' — the constant that DEFINES the standard; change it and the spec is no longer doing this standard, so an editor must not offer it. 'bounded' — a limit the spec may make stricter but never looser; the bound present (max or min) is the loosest the standard permits. 'optional' — the standard names the field but sets no value; the spec decides. 'not_applicable' — the standard says a value must not be stated for this content class.

value.description: Required when rule is 'locked': the defining constant.

max.description: Loosest permitted value where looser means greater (tolerance, a true-peak ceiling). A spec may go lower.

min.description: Loosest permitted value where looser means smaller. A spec may go higher.

cite.description: Where in the document the constraint is stated, precise enough to find: clause letter, section number, table.

quote.description: Verbatim text of the cited passage. The constraint is checkable against the document without re-reading the whole of it.

note.description: Anything the numbers alone would misrepresent — an exception, a conditional, a 'should' rather than a 'shall'.
